definitions.explanation: A projectile fired from a cannon or artillery piece. Also used more broadly for any large-caliber ammunition.

examples.japanese: {砲弾|ほうだん}が{飛|と}んできた。
{不発弾|ふはつだん}の{砲弾|ほうだん}が{工事現場|こうじげんば}で{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: An unexploded shell was found at the construction site.

examples.japanese: {戦時中|せんじちゅう}、この{町|まち}には{何百発|なんびゃっぱつ}もの{砲弾|ほうだん}が{撃|う}ち{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: During the war, hundreds of shells were fired into this town.

notes: Composed of {砲|ほう} (cannon, artillery) + {弾|だん} (bullet, projectile). Common collocations: {砲弾|ほうだん}が{着弾|ちゃくだん}する (a shell lands/hits), {砲弾|ほうだん}を{撃|う}ち{込|こ}む (to fire shells into), {砲弾|ほうだん}の{雨|あめ} (a rain of shells). In Japan, {不発弾|ふはつだん} (unexploded ordnance) from World War II are still occasionally found during construction, especially in Okinawa. The counter for shells is {発|はつ}: {一発|いっぱつ}の{砲弾|ほうだん} (one shell).
